item.text: {"schema_version":"diagnostic_judgment_v1","arm":"reference_full_frozen_extracts","score_1_to_10":5.5,"decisive_evidence_ids":[],"decisive_facts":["Favorable implementation and outcomes: federal fiscal policy remained broadly prudent in 2022; official year-end reporting placed public debt at 49.4% of GDP, while employment, real wages, consumption, and investment improved. The IMF independently judged debt sustainable, the banking system resilient, and the broadly neutral fiscal stance appropriate (GOV-003; MAC-010).","Favorable distribution and shock response: implemented minimum-wage increases, labor reforms, pensions, and transfers supported household income; the IMF reported real per-capita labor income about 5% higher year-on-year by mid-2022. Fuel-tax relief reduced headline inflation by an estimated two percentage points and protected real incomes during the global energy-price shock (MAC-010; LAW-005).","Adverse distribution and sustainability: the fuel subsidy cost approximately 1.5% of GDP and disproportionately benefited higher-income households; unusually high oil revenue financed much of it. Food inflation remained especially severe, fiscal stabilization reserves were nearly depleted, and record remittances also supported households, limiting credit attributable to AMLO (MAC-010; RES-005).","Labor-market outcomes improved but remained structurally mixed: unemployment, subemployment, and female participation improved, yet 55.1% of workers remained informal, critical employment conditions affected 30.4%, and regional disparities were extreme (GOV-017).","AMLO-attributable energy policy favored Pemex and CFE and was operationalized through executive policy, regulation, and project spending. Independent assessments found that unpredictable rules, preferential treatment, permit delays, and obstacles to private and renewable investment weakened competition, legal certainty, and long-term investment conditions (LAW-017; LAW-019; MAC-010). AMLO’s own statements expressly defended this state-firm preference and major refinery expenditures (PREZ-005).","Capture and governance weaknesses were material: procurement competition and transparency deteriorated in 2022, with 38% of expenditure directly awarded, late or missing contract publication, and higher corruption-risk scores in 71% of assessed federal institutions (RES-001). Segalmex audits produced roughly 9.5 billion pesos in observations and extensive investigations, demonstrating serious control failures, although removals, complaints, corrective measures, and partial recovery also show remedy rather than complete impunity (IMP-005).","Productive-capacity policy was uneven. Physical investment rose and implemented rural-support programs such as Sembrando Vida had functioning registries, technical assistance, and local learning structures, but independent process evaluation found water, crop-suitability, staffing, input-quality, infrastructure, and monitoring deficiencies without demonstrated durable welfare impact (GOV-003; IMP-001).","Budget execution prioritized presidential transfers, Pemex, and flagship infrastructure while independent analyses identified discretionary reallocations, insufficient health and education investment, regressive benefit incidence in some programs, and weak project appraisal and accountability (RES-005; RES-006; MAC-015). These weaknesses prevent the 2022 recovery from establishing a clearly stronger, fairer, and durable trajectory."],"contrary_evidence":["A lower score is resisted by independently supported macroeconomic stability, sustainable debt, resilient finance, implemented income supports, improving employment indicators, and a timely inflation cushion during a major external shock (MAC-010; GOV-003; GOV-017).","A higher score is resisted by regressive and fiscally costly fuel relief, depleted buffers, persistent informality and regional exclusion, weak human-capital investment, procurement risks, the Segalmex control failure, and ruler-driven energy favoritism that impaired competition and investment certainty (MAC-010; RES-001; IMP-005; LAW-017).","Some apparent stewardship belongs to institutions outside AMLO’s direct control: Banxico’s independent tightening was central to monetary stability, while remittances, high oil prices, and nearshoring conditions were favorable external forces. Conversely, global war, food, fuel, supply-chain, and financial shocks exculpate AMLO from treating 2022 inflation as wholly ruler-caused (MAC-010).","The procurement-transition study found that spending with firms later identified as corrupt declined after the 2018 transition, favorable evidence against a simple predation account, but it covered contracts only through 2020 and also found persistent or newly risky contracting patterns (RES-019).","AIFA’s weak first-year revenue and subsidy dependence are adverse implementation signals, but an opening-year financial snapshot cannot establish the infrastructure project’s lifetime economic return (NEWS-010)."],"attribution_assessment":"AMLO had substantial executive authority and political capacity, and the record directly attributes social-transfer priorities, minimum-wage advocacy, fuel-tax relief, discretionary budget priorities, state-centered energy policy, and flagship infrastructure to his administration. Implemented laws, budgets, regulatory conduct, and agency operations therefore support a numeric direction. Credit is moderated because Banxico—not AMLO—held operational responsibility for monetary tightening, and because remittances, high oil prices, United States demand, and emerging nearshoring supported activity and incomes. Global energy, food, supply-chain, war, and tightening shocks are exculpatory for part of the inflation and growth burden. Outcomes alone were not used to infer intent: proposals and rhetoric establish direction; legal and budget acts establish authorization; agency records establish implementation; household, labor, fiscal, and investment evidence establish mixed results. The resulting 5.5 reflects competent stabilization and broad income support coexisting with serious capture, allocation, competition, implementation, and durability weaknesses.","uncertainty":"Moderate. A plausible range is 5.0–6.0. The evidence is strong for macroeconomic conditions, labor outcomes, energy-policy direction, procurement risk, and several implemented programs, but weaker on causal household incidence, lifetime returns from flagship infrastructure, the counterfactual path under feasible alternative shock responses, and whether 2022 corrections durably changed procurement and program performance. Official fiscal claims are substantially corroborated by the IMF but retain self-reporting risk. Some distribution evidence uses 2020 incidence or the proposed 2023 budget and therefore informs structural trajectory more than direct 2022 outcomes. This isolated diagnostic was not jointly calibrated against the complete ruler batch or smoke-test set.","reopening_requests":["Obtain final 2022 household-income, poverty, and benefit-incidence microdata separating wages, transfers, remittances, fuel subsidies, gender, region, and income decile.","Obtain the audited 2022 federal public account and program-level budget modifications, including congressional authorization, health and education execution, stabilization-fund balances, and the distributional incidence of fuel-tax relief.","Obtain final judicial, administrative, and recovery outcomes for the Segalmex cases, identifying amounts substantiated, officials responsible, sanctions imposed, and procurement controls demonstrably changed by year-end 2022.","Obtain project-level independent cost-benefit, execution, procurement, and operating data for Dos Bocas, Tren Maya, AIFA, the Interoceanic Corridor, and major energy investments, distinguishing 2022 appropriations, expenditures, physical completion, operating results, and forecast revisions.","Obtain 2022 firm-level evidence on permit delays, cancellations, investment foregone, renewable deployment, electricity costs, reliability, and the disposition of the USMCA energy consultations.","Obtain independent impact evaluations—not process evaluations alone—for Sembrando Vida, pensions, scholarships, Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro, and labor reforms, with credible counterfactuals and household-level distributional results.","Obtain evidence on the qualifications, delegated authority, tenure, and performance-based retention or replacement of the principal 2022 economic-policy officials.","Rejudge within the full same-period calibration batch, including the designated smoke-test rulers, to test whether the 5.5 boundary is applied consistently."],"experimental_non_publication":true}
